craft_claim: Laughter requires a degree of emotional distance; too much proximity to real stakes suppresses the comic response, so psychic distance is a controllable craft dial.

supporting_evidence.note: Bergson identifies an 'absence of feeling' or indifference as a condition of laughter and names emotion as its enemy; laughter is a social gesture rather than a personal emotional reaction.
Psychological distance is one of the named routes by which a potential violation becomes benign and therefore humorous.

counterevidence.note: Section B lists psychological distance as only one of three routes to benign-ness, alongside an alternative norm and weak commitment to the violated norm, so distance is a sufficient route rather than a required one and humour can hold at close range where another route supplies benignity.

scope: Narrator positioning and psychic distance in prose and copy; comic staging of tense material.
exceptions: Dark or gallows humour can operate close to real pain when the framing still grants distance or shared solidarity.
Empathic identification with a target can be the intended effect in tragicomic work, which is not pure comedic tone.
